title: Electrical safety
description: Recognize hazards and know when to stop.

cards.title: Use a generator safely
cards.summary: Portable generators can produce deadly carbon monoxide and can backfeed a home circuit if connected incorrectly.
steps: Operate the generator outdoors, well away from windows, doors, and vents.
Never run one in a home, garage, basement, or enclosed porch.
Use outdoor-rated extension cords in good condition and within their rating.
Have a qualified electrician install any transfer switch; never plug a generator into a wall outlet.
cards.source: Electrical Safety Foundation International: portable generators

cards.title: Water and electricity
cards.summary: Water-damaged electrical gear can remain dangerous after it dries. Avoid flooded areas and have a qualified professional inspect affected equipment.
steps: Stay away from downed power lines and flooded electrical equipment.
Do not touch a breaker or fuse with wet hands or while standing on a wet surface.
Leave flooded areas until the utility confirms power is off.
Have water-damaged outlets, breakers, and appliances inspected before reuse.

cards.title: Spot an unsafe extension cord
cards.summary: Extension cords are temporary tools, not permanent wiring. A damaged, warm, or overloaded cord needs attention.
steps: Check the cord and plug for cracks, exposed wire, or heat before use.
Choose a cord rated for the appliance and intended location.
Do not route a cord under rugs or through a doorway where it can be pinched.
For a permanent need, ask a qualified electrician to add a suitable outlet.
